transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’ve gotten kind of stuck doing these little routines. I’ll wash my hands again after handling my wrist brace, or I’ll go back and recheck the stove and the front door. Sometimes I silently count through steps before I leave the house. I know I’ve usually already done enough, but I still end up doing it, and it’s starting to make me late.
Do these routines cause you significant distress or interfere with your daily life?

Yes, some. I’m still managing on my own, but it does get in the way. I’ve been late to my docent shifts because I can’t get out the door on time, and I’ve skipped a few museum events just because the whole process of leaving felt like too much.
Do you have unwanted thoughts or ideas that keep repeating in your mind?

Yes. I’ll be reading at home or getting ready to go to the museum, and a thought just pushes in—like maybe I left something unsafe, or touched something dirty, or somehow put someone else at risk. I know it’s probably out of proportion, but it keeps coming back anyway.
Do you feel like you're doing these routines to make those unwanted thoughts go away?

Yes, I think that’s mostly what it is. The thought comes up that something’s unsafe or not clean, and then I feel like I have to do the routine—wash again, check the stove or door again, count through the steps—just to quiet it down. Even when I know I probably already did enough, I still end up doing it, and then I’m late.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform these routines to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes. That’s the feeling behind a lot of it. If I don’t wash after handling my wrist brace, or if I don’t recheck the stove or the front door, I get this worry that something could go wrong. So I end up counting through the steps again before I leave, even though part of me knows I’ve already done enough. It’s not severe, but it does make me late.
Do you feel like your routines are also done to prevent something bad from happening to someone else?

Yes, sometimes that’s part of it. I’ll think, if I don’t wash again or check the stove or the front door, maybe I could put someone else at risk somehow. So I go back through it, or count the steps in my head before I leave, even when I know I already did enough. It’s not extreme, but it does make me late.
Do you ever feel the need to arrange things in a specific order or symmetry?

Not really arranging things, no. It’s more that I get stuck doing certain steps before I can move on—like washing again, rechecking the stove or front door, or silently counting through what I’ve done before I leave. Even when I know it should be enough, I feel pulled to do it again, and that’s what’s making me late.
Do you feel like your routines are also done to prevent something bad from happening to yourself?

Yes, I think so. It’s that feeling that if I don’t wash again after touching my wrist brace, or if I don’t check the stove or the front door one more time, something could happen to me. I know I’ve probably already done enough, but I still feel like I have to go through it again, or count the steps in my head before I leave. It’s not constant, but it’s enough that I end up running late.
Do you ever feel the need to repeat a routine because something feels 'not just right' or asymmetrical?

Not so much because things look uneven or out of order. It’s more that I get stuck repeating the routine—washing again after the wrist brace, checking the stove or the front door, or counting through the steps before I leave. Even when I know I already did it, it still feels like I haven’t quite done enough, and then I end up late.
Do you feel like your routines are aimed at preventing harm caused by something specific that you are worried about?

It’s not really one specific thing I can point to. It’s more that I get uneasy that if I don’t do the routine again—wash after handling my wrist brace, check the stove or the front door, count through the steps before I leave—then I haven’t done enough and something might be missed. Even when I know I already checked, I still feel pushed to repeat it, and that’s what’s been making me late.
Is there something specific that you are worried about when you feel the need to repeat these routines?

Yes, usually it’s a vague worry that I’ve left something unsafe, or touched something unclean, or somehow put someone else at risk. Like if I’m reading at home or getting ready to go to the museum, that thought just barges in, even though I know it’s probably out of proportion.
Do you feel like your routines are attempts to directly prevent harm from occurring to yourself or others?

I think so, yes, at least that’s what it feels like in the moment. I wash again after touching my wrist brace, or I recheck the stove and the front door, or count through what I need to do before leaving. It’s like I’m trying to make sure nothing bad happens or nothing gets missed, even though part of me knows I’ve already done enough. It’s been making me late.
Have you had to stop or significantly reduce any activities or responsibilities because of these routines or unwanted thoughts?

I haven’t had to stop everything or anything like that. I’m still managing on my own. But it has made me late to my docent shifts, and I’ve skipped a few museum events because just getting out the door felt like too much.
Do you feel like your routines are attempts to prevent harm from occurring due to something you might have done or not done?

Yes. That’s pretty much how it feels. I get stuck thinking that if I don’t wash again after handling my wrist brace, or if I don’t recheck the stove or the front door, then something might happen because I missed something. So I go through those steps again, even when I know I’ve already done enough, and then I end up running late.
Is there a specific bad outcome that you're trying to prevent when you do these routines?

Mostly it’s this feeling that if I don’t do it, I’ll miss something important and something bad could happen. Like if I don’t recheck the stove or the front door, or if I don’t wash again after touching my wrist brace, I can’t quite let it go. I know I’ve probably already done enough, but I still feel like I have to run through it again before I leave.
